original_value: Spectrum handoff is one of the key techniques in a cognitive radio system. In order to improve the agility and the reliability of spectrum handoffs as well as the system throughput in hybrid cognitive radio networks (HCRNs) combing interweave mode with underlay mode, a predictive (or proactive) spectrum handoff scheme based on a deep Q-network (DQN) for HCRNs is proposed in this paper. In the proposed spectrum handoff approach, spectrum handoff success rate is introduced into an optimal spectrum resource allocation model to ensure the reliability of spectrum handoff, and the closed-form expression for the spectrum handoff success rate is obtained based on the Poisson distribution. Furthermore, we exploit the transfer learning strategy to further improve the DQN learning process and finally achieve a priority sequence of target available channels for spectrum handoffs, which can maximize the overall HCRNs throughput while satisfying constraints on secondary users’ interference with primary user, limits on the spectrum handoff success rate, and the secondary users’ performance requirements. Simulation results show that the proposed spectrum handoff scheme outperforms the state-of-the-art spectrum handoff algorithms based on predictive decision in terms of the convergence rate, the handoff success rate and the system throughput.

result.paraphrase: Spectrum handoff is a key technique in cognitive radio systems. To enhance the agility and reliability of spectrum handoffs, as well as overall throughput, in hybrid cognitive radio networks (HCRNs) that combine interweave and underlay modes, this paper proposes a predictive, or proactive, spectrum handoff scheme for HCRNs based on a deep Q-network (DQN). In the proposed approach, spectrum handoff success rate is incorporated into an optimal spectrum resource allocation model to guarantee handoff reliability, and a closed-form expression for the handoff success rate is derived from the Poisson distribution. Moreover, transfer learning is used to further improve the DQN training process, ultimately producing a priority ordering of candidate available channels for spectrum handoffs that can maximize total HCRN throughput while meeting constraints on secondary-user interference to the primary user, spectrum handoff success rate limits, and secondary-user performance requirements. Simulation results indicate that the proposed scheme outperforms state-of-the-art predictive decision-based spectrum handoff algorithms in convergence rate, handoff success rate, and system throughput.
